[text-37] list item "README"
[text-38] list item "Contributing"
[text-39] list item "Security"
[text-40] heading "The Free Software Media System"
[text-41] "Jellyfin is a Free Software Media System that puts you in control of managing and streaming your media. It is an alternative to the proprietary Emby and Plex, to provide media from a dedicated server to end-user devices via multiple apps. Jellyfin is descended from Emby's 3.5.2 release and ported to"
[text-42] "There are no strings attached, no premium licenses or features, and no hidden agendas: just a team that wants to build something better and work together to achieve it. We welcome anyone who is interested in joining us in our quest!"
[text-43] "For further details, please see our documentation page. To receive the latest updates, get help with Jellyfin, and join the community, please visit one of our communication channels. For more information about the project, please see our about page."
[text-44] "Want to get started? Check out our downloads page or our installation guide, then see our quick start guide. You can also build from source."
[text-45] "Something not working right? Open an Issue on GitHub."
[text-46] "Want to contribute? Check out our contributing choose-your-own-adventure to see where you can help, then see our contributing guide and our community standards."
[text-47] "New idea or improvement? Check out our feature request hub."
[text-48] "Don't see Jellyfin in your language? Check out our Weblate instance to help translate Jellyfin and its subprojects."
[text-49] heading "Jellyfin Server"
[text-50] "This repository contains the code for Jellyfin's backend server. Note that this is only one of many projects under the Jellyfin GitHub organization on GitHub. If you want to contribute, you can start by checking out our documentation to see what to work on."
[text-51] heading "Server Development"
[text-52] "These instructions will help you get set up with a local development environment in order to contribute to this repository. Before you start, please be sure to completely read our guidelines on development contributions. Note that this project is supported on all major operating systems except FreeB"
[text-53] heading "Prerequisites"
[text-54] "Before the project can be built, you must first install the .NET 10 SDK on your system."
[text-55] "Instructions to run this project from the command line are included here, but you will also need to install an IDE if you want to debug the server while it is running. Any IDE that supports .NET 6 development will work, but two options are recent versions of Visual Studio (at least 2022) and Visual "
[text-56] "ffmpeg will also need to be installed."
[text-57] heading "Cloning the Repository"
[text-58] "After dependencies have been installed you will need to clone a local copy of this repository. If you just want to run the server from source you can clone this repository directly, but if you are intending to contribute code changes to the project, you should set up your own fork of the repository."
[text-59] code "git clone https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin.git"
[text-60] heading "Installing the Web Client"
[text-61] "The server is configured to host the static files required for the web client in addition to serving the backend by default. Before you can run the server, you will need to get a copy of the web client since they are not included in this repository directly."
[text-62] "Note that it is recommended for development to host the web client separately from the web server with some additional configuration, in which case you can skip this step."
[text-63] "There are two options to get the files for the web client."
[text-64] list item "Build them from source following the instructions on the jellyfin-web repository"
[text-65] list item "Get the pre-built files from an existing installation of the server. For example, with a Windows server installation the client files are located at C:\\Program Files\\Jellyfin\\Server\\jellyfin-web"
[text-66] heading "Running The Server"
[text-67] "The following instructions will help you get the project up and running via the command line, or your preferred IDE."
[text-68] "To run the project with Visual Studio you can open the Solution (.sln) file and then press F5 to run the server."
[text-69] "To run the project with Visual Studio Code you will first need to open the repository directory with Visual Studio Code using the Open Folder... option."
[text-70] "Second, you need to install the recommended extensions for the workspace. Note that extension recommendations are classified as either \"Workspace Recommendations\" or \"Other Recommendations\", but only the \"Workspace Recommendations\" are required."
[text-71] "After the required extensions are installed, you can run the server by pressing F5."
[text-72] "To run the server from the command line you can use the dotnet run command. The example below shows how to do this if you have cloned the repository into a directory named jellyfin (the default directory name) and should work on all operating systems."
[text-73] code "cd jellyfin                          # Move into the repository directory\ndotnet run --project Jellyfin.Server --webdir /absolute/path/to/jellyfin-web/dist # Run the server startup project"
[text-74] "A second option is to build the project and then run the resulting executable file directly. When running the executable directly you can easily add command line options. Add the --help flag to list details on all the supported command line options."
[text-75] list item "Build the project"
[text-76] code "dotnet build                       # Build the project\ncd Jellyfin.Server/bin/Debug/net10.0 # Change into the build output directory"
[text-77] list item "Execute the build output. On Linux, Mac, etc. use ./jellyfin and on Windows use jellyfin.exe."
[text-78] "If the Server is configured to host the Web Client, and the Server is running, the Web Client can be accessed at http://localhost:8096 by default."
[text-79] "API documentation can be viewed at http://localhost:8096/api-docs/swagger/index.html"
[text-80] heading "Running from GitHub Codespaces"
[text-81] "As Jellyfin will run on a container on a GitHub hosted server, JF needs to handle some things differently."
[text-82] "NOTE: Depending on the selected configuration (if you just click 'create codespace' it will create a default configuration one) it might take 20-30 seconds to load all extensions and prepare the environment while VS Code is already open. Just give it some time and wait until you see Downloading .NET"
[text-83] "NOTE: If you want to access the JF instance from outside, like with a WebClient on another PC, remember to set the \"ports\" in the lower VS Code window to public."
[text-84] "NOTE: When first opening the server instance with any WebUI, you will be sent to the login instead of the setup page. Refresh the login page once and you should be redirected to the Setup."
[text-85] "There are two configurations for you to choose from."
[text-86] "This creates a container that has everything to run and debug the Jellyfin Media server but does not setup anything else. Each time you create a new container you have to run through the whole setup again. There is also no ffmpeg, webclient or media preloaded. Use the .NET Launch (nowebclient) launc"
[text-87] "Keep in mind that as this has no web client you have to connect to it via an external client. This can be just another codespace container running the WebUI. vuejs does not work from the get-go as it does not support the setup steps."
[text-88] "this extends the default server with a default installation of ffmpeg6 though the means described here: https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/installation/linux#repository-manual If you want to install a specific ffmpeg version, follow the comments embedded in the .devcontainer/Dev - Server Ffmpeg/insta"
[text-89] "Use the ghcs .NET Launch (nowebclient, ffmpeg) launch config to run with the jellyfin-ffmpeg enabled."
[text-90] heading "Running The Tests"
[text-91] "This repository also includes unit tests that are used to validate functionality as part of a CI pipeline on Azure. There are several ways to run these tests."
[text-92] list item "Run tests from the command line using dotnet test"
[text-93] list item "Run tests in Visual Studio using the Test Explorer"
[text-94] list item "Run individual tests in Visual Studio Code using the associated CodeLens annotation"
[text-95] heading "Advanced Configuration"
[text-96] "The following sections describe some more advanced scenarios for running the server from source that build upon the standard instructions above."
[text-97] "It is not necessary to host the frontend web client as part of the backend server. Hosting these two components separately may be useful for frontend developers who would prefer to host the client in a separate webpack development server for a tighter development loop. See the jellyfin-web repo for "
[text-98] "To instruct the server not to host the web content, there is a nowebclient configuration flag that must be set. This can be specified using the command line switch --nowebclient or the environment variable JELLYFIN_NOWEBCONTENT=true."
[text-99] "Since this is a common scenario, there is also a separate launch profile defined for Visual Studio called Jellyfin.Server (nowebcontent) that can be selected from the 'Start Debugging' dropdown in the main toolbar."
[text-100] "NOTE: The setup wizard cannot be run if the web client is hosted separately."

options.scroll_down: scroll the page down a screen, when no block further down holds what the words ask for
options.back: go back to the previous page
options.press: press a key: enter, escape, space or an arrow key
options.read: read the page aloud or show its contents
options.clear: clear the text in the focused field
options.stop: stop what the browser is doing
options.none: not a command for this page: a remark, a question, a name, noise
options.play: music: find a song or video by the words and play it now, on YouTube or on this site as the words point — never the page's play button, which is a click
options.play_next: music: find a song by the words and play it after the one playing
options.queue: music: find a song by the words and add it to the end of the queue
options.say_time: appliance: say the time and date — 19:25, Friday 23 October
options.say_weather: appliance: say today's weather in the home city — words naming another place or a website are a search, not this — no forecast yet
options.say_playing: appliance: say the song playing — nothing playing
options.say_timer: appliance: say how long is left on the timer — no timer set

slot.instructions: Which words of the transcript are the thing the command carries verbatim: the address to open, the search terms, the song to play, the text to type, the key to press? Never the command word itself: "play X" carries X. A line with no command word, such as a question, carries itself: its search terms are the line as asked. Choose none when it carries none.

options.none: the command carries no words of its own

extent.instructions: Only when the action scrolls the page or a scrolling part of it: how far? Choose words when the words give a number of screens or pages; screen when they say nothing of how far. Ignored for every other action.

options.words: as many screens as the number the words carry
options.little: a little: a third of a screen
options.screen: one screen, as Page Down does
options.end: all the way: to the bottom, or to the top going up

where.instructions: Where do the words point: at something on this page, at something on github.com that is not on this page, or somewhere else on the web?

options.page: on this page: one of the numbered refs
options.site: on github.com but not on this page: a page, a person, a post, a section of it
options.web: elsewhere: another website, or a search of the whole web
